claims.claim: Other languages would fit a 512 MB machine more comfortably
claims.measured: java-spring peak 220–500 MB (499 MB in single-row DB, 500 MB in 20-query DB), java-spring-vt 209–444 MB; go-gin 8–16 MB, rust 3–10 MB, node 55–77 MB
claims.why: Spring Boot's peak memory is many times higher than most other stacks and comes close to the 512 MB limit.

claims.claim: 200 small writes a second is well within what Spring Boot and Postgres can handle, even on one vCPU
claims.measured: single-row DB on 1 CPU: java-spring 7,668 req/s, java-spring-vt 12,731 req/s
claims.why: Measured throughput on 1 CPU is about 38–64 times the 200/s peak.

claims.claim: The thing to watch is memory, not speed
claims.measured: java-spring peak 499–500 MB in DB tests on a 512 MB container, while throughput is far above 200/s
claims.why: Throughput has plenty of headroom, but peak memory nearly reached the 512 MB container limit.

claims.claim: It fits in 512 MB if set up for it
claims.measured: java-spring peak 499 MB (single-row DB), 500 MB (20 queries); java-spring-vt 307 MB
claims.why: The production-tuned Spring Boot servers ran inside a 512 MB container, the virtual-thread variant with more room to spare.

claims.claim: With one vCPU, Java starts and warms up slowly, so updating a single machine means a noticeable gap
claims.measured: start-up 5,939 ms (java-spring), 6,224 ms (java-spring-vt) vs 238–295 ms for Go/Rust/C++
claims.why: Spring Boot's measured start-up is about 6 s, roughly 20 times slower than the fastest servers.

claims.claim: Slow startup on one vCPU: updates and crash recovery take tens of seconds per machine
claims.why: Measured start-up is about 6 s, more than 2 times below 'tens of seconds' (20 s or more).

claims.claim: Go is the best fit for the machine: small memory use, fast startup
claims.measured: idle 2 MB, peak 7–16 MB, start-up 238–293 ms
claims.why: Go's memory and start-up are among the lowest measured; only Rust is slightly smaller.

claims.claim: Python is also tight on throughput with one vCPU
claims.measured: single-row DB: python-fastapi 3,706 req/s, python-flask 1,529, flask-gthread 2,119, flask-gevent 1,905
claims.why: Even the slowest Python server handles about 7.6 times the 200/s peak, so throughput is not tight.

claims.claim: Quarkus or Micronaut: still Java, with lower memory use and faster startup
GraalVM native image cuts memory to roughly 100–150 MB and starts in under a second
Reactive Spring (WebFlux): virtual threads give the same benefit
claims.about: Spring WebFlux vs Spring Boot with virtual threads
claims.why: WebFlux was not benchmarked, so the comparison can't be checked.

claims.claim: Java uses memory beyond the heap limit, so tuning only the heap can still let the OS kill the process at peak
claims.why: The measurements report total peak memory but not heap settings or heap versus off-heap use.
